title: Ernest Boehringer and playing silent-film comedies at the Triangle Theater
summary: Boehringer managed the Triangle Theater. Leclerc played comedies on piano with a drummer doing effects, while Tony Parenti played the dramas.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Oh, this back of your Triangle Jazz Blues, who is Ernest Boehringer? It's dedicated to you.

He was the manager of the Triangle Theater. Oh. Yeah. And you... You said Boehringer, I had to start to think for a while. Yeah, Ernest Boehringer. Oh yes, he was a wonderful little fella in those days. Yeah, he was the manager of the Triangle Theater. And I used to play the comedies in those days, you know. And Tony Parenti, a little parent, he used to play with the orchestra, he used to play the other stuff, you know. The dramas and so forth and on.
Did you play with the films at all, with silent movies?

Oh yeah, yeah. I played the film on all of the... In other words, a fella by name... I'm trying to think of his name too, I can't. He was up in the country, Donaldsonville, I forget it was. And he and I, he played the drum and I played the piano. We featured all the comedies. And he used to put all the effects in, you know. He was a drummer? Yeah, he was a drummer. I played the piano and he played the drummer. Or rather he played the drums. And he put all the effects in and he was marvelous at that. He was a big, big, big fella. He later died too. He died young. Yeah, I remember those days.
